claim: Functionally separated real-model interaction can form an accepted actionable condition or joint solution unavailable before interaction and materially better than simpler fair baselines.
updated_status: weakened; not supported in source-identity task
scope: one local collapsible Harness engineering task
what_it_distinguishes: formation versus discovery and unclosed candidate negotiation
what_it_does_not_distinguish: tasks with non-collapsible real authority or long-term transfer
theory_consequence: Do not infer formation from interaction; require signature, adoption, ablation, and positive net value.
engineering_consequence: Use A2A for unresolved authority/acceptance only after simpler engineering and central queries.
next_discriminating_action: Choose a real task whose authority or liability cannot safely collapse and run a paired target-domain adoption test.

claim: A fair least-privilege central coordinator is sufficient or superior when task-relevant context and authority are collapsible.
updated_status: partially supported for conflict discovery; synthesis Unknown
what_it_distinguishes: central query sufficiency versus dynamic interaction for surfacing owner conflict
what_it_does_not_distinguish: whether a healthy shorter central builder would produce an adoptable synthesis
theory_consequence: Sovereign A2A remains conditional; repeated transport failure cannot be counted as central reasoning failure.
engineering_consequence: Use shorter or streaming structured synthesis and preserve runtime failures separately.
next_discriminating_action: Preregister a shorter output protocol with the same owner reports and an independent runtime.

claim: Model-context isolation plus tool/authority mediation can create a functional experimental boundary without relying only on role wording.
updated_status: supported only as benign functional separation
scope: tool-less local Claude sessions mediated by a trusted root
what_it_distinguishes: functional context confinement versus pure role wording
what_it_does_not_distinguish: adversarial isolation, OS security, privacy from root, or sovereign organization
theory_consequence: Treat context separation and sovereignty as separate claims.
engineering_consequence: Keep no-tool conformance and explicit trusted-root limitations in experiment design.
next_discriminating_action: Replay on independent OS/container identities only if a future claim requires adversarial or organizational isolation.
